sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- operator statement via Reuters, Nov 6] One seafarer was killed in an explosion believed to have been caused by a missile attack on the Marshall Islands-flagged product tanker MT Velos Sapphire (74,998 dwt, Greek-managed, built 2007) in the Arabian Gulf on Thursday Nov 4. The vessel was sailing unladen from Fujairah (departed Nov 3) toward Sitra, Bahrain, when struck ~50 nautical miles north of Qatar's Madinat ash Shamal at 23:20 UTC. The crew member was initially reported missing, then found fatally injured on board. No other crew injured; fire extinguished; no pollution reported; vessel taken to Bahrain's Khalifa Bin Salman Port; investigation to be launched. [VERIFIED FACT -- UKMTO warning 196-26] Two unidentified projectiles hit an unnamed tanker at 23:20 UTC at that position; operator subsequently reported an explosion on the aft port side, believed caused by an unidentified missile. [ATTRIBUTED -- IMO via Splash247 / Outlook India] IMO identified the vessel, recording damage, no pollution and one seafarer missing; IMO's latest figures: 129 confirmed maritime incidents across the region, 24 seafarer fatalities since the conflict began. [ATTRIBUTED -- Seatrade Maritime] Seven vessels reported struck in the region since the beginning of November; Velos Sapphire was the second incident inside the Arabian Gulf after chemical/product tanker Largo Atom (struck by two unknown projectiles Nov 1). Other November incidents: offshore tug Selat Storm, bulker Era S, dhow Al Jusufi. [ATTRIBUTED -- Splash247] Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority reshuffled its Hormuz blacklist: 239 vessels now listed (down from 240 earlier in the week, sharply up from 77 in September); two US-sanctioned LPG carriers removed. Velos Sapphire itself is NOT on the blacklist; sister ship Velos Amber is listed, with no established connection to the attack. [ANALYSIS -- Maritime Executive] The strike location is far from Hormuz, consistent with an apparent strategy to attack targets outside the American security umbrella around the Musandam Peninsula. [PORTWATCH GAP -- STALE] Newest IMF PortWatch snapshot remains portwatch-2026-10-26.json, stale=true, latest observation 2026-10-18 (Hormuz 4 transits, 7-day avg 3.71 vs 2025 baseline 85.53/day). Do NOT cite that count as current. Current counted figures are JMIC 111 (4 attacks in 96h, Nov 1-3, off Musandam; recorded 1000-01) and IMO (129 incidents / 24 fatalities as of Nov 6).
sections.what_verified: 4 distinct publisher families with declared tiers carry the operator-confirmed death: Reuters (T1) + Arab News (T3) + Al Arabiya (T3, STATE SA) + Gulf News (T3, liveblog entry 18:15 ). Straits Times (T3) carries the same Reuters wire = 1 family with Reuters. Splash247, Seatrade Maritime, Maritime Executive, Outlook India, Business Recorder, Devdiscourse and Duke FM have NO declared tier in the registry -- attribution only, NOT counted. UKMTO (T1) + IMO (T1) corroborate the incident as official incident reports.
sections.what_disputed: No group has claimed the strike and no independent attribution exists; the 'missile' cause is the operator's belief ('believed to have been caused by'), not a confirmed weapon identification. Iran's IRGC claimed mine strikes on tankers near Hormuz (recorded 1300-01) but has not claimed this Gulf incident. The vessel was NOT on Iran's blacklist, weakening any blacklist-enforcement reading. IMO had listed the seafarer as missing, not confirmed dead, before the operator's Friday statement.
sections.why_matters: A seafarer is dead in the Gulf -- not at Hormuz, 50 miles off Qatar. The shipping war just moved outside the escort bubble, 7 ships hit since November 1, and Tehran's blacklist just hit 239 vessels.

totw_analysis: Our read: A seafarer is dead in the Gulf -- not at Hormuz, 50 miles off Qatar. The shipping war just moved outside the escort bubble, 7 ships hit since November 1, and Tehran's blacklist just hit 239 vessels. The fault line our audience is arguing over: The war has come to the open Gulf -- a tanker 50 miles off Qatar, hundreds of miles west of Hormuz and outside the US escort bubble. Is the American shield failing, or was this ship outside the shield by choice -- and who is doing the shooting when nobody claims it?
